candidates.claim: rtr-01 has a static route 198.18.0.0/15 via 198.51.100.1 that is not in the approved baseline.
candidates.remediation: Confirm the route with the engineer and either add it to the approved baseline or remove it.

candidates.claim: Trunks sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 and Gi1/0/24 carry VLAN 10, while the registry says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10 and these trunks are not OT-facing ports.
candidates.remediation: Engineer to confirm whether VLAN 10 on these two uplink trunks is an approved exception; if not, remove VLAN 10 from their allowed lists.

candidates.claim: rtr-01 has a leg in MGMT (GigabitEthernet0 10.10.99.12/24) and two default routes, one via the ISP and one via fw-01's MGMT address 10.10.99.1; its interface record shows no acl_in, so the records do not rule out forwarding between MGMT and OUTSIDE outside fw-01 policy.
candidates.remediation: Confirm the intended routing for rtr-01 and remove the MGMT leg or the default route via 10.10.99.1 if it is not needed.

clarifications.question: Is rtr-01 meant to have a leg in MGMT (GigabitEthernet0 10.10.99.12/24) and a default route via 10.10.99.1 alongside its ISP default route? If so, which hosts use rtr-01 as a path, and which ACL controls MGMT-to-OUTSIDE traffic on that path?

The registry says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10, yet the approved trunks sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 {10,99} and Gi1/0/24 {10,20,30,99} carry VLAN 10. Are these two uplink trunks an approved exception to the OT-facing rule?
